chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Barqī, from Abū Hāshim Dāwūd ibn al-Qāsim al-Jaʿfarī, from Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī (عليه السلام), who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) came, and with him was al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), while he was leaning on the hand of Salmān. He entered al-Masjid al-Ḥarām and sat down, when a man of fine appearance and clothing approached, greeted Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and he returned the greeting. The man sat and then said: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I ask you about three matters. If you inform me of them, I will know that the people have undertaken regarding your affair that which has been decreed against them, and that they are not secure in their worldly life and their Hereafter. But if it is otherwise, I will know that you and they are equal in the matter.”

Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) said to him: “Ask me whatever appears to you.” He said: “Inform me about a man: when he sleeps, where does his spirit go? And about a man: how does he remember and forget? And about a man: how does his child resemble the paternal uncles and the maternal uncles?” Then Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) turned to al-Ḥasan and said: “O Abā Muḥammad, answer him.”

He said: al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام) answered him. Then the man said: “I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I have never ceased bearing witness to it. And I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), and I have never ceased bearing witness to that. And I bear witness that you are the وصي of the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) and the one who upholds his proof”—and he pointed to Amīr al-Muʾminīn—“and I have never ceased bearing witness to it. And I bear witness that you are his وصي and the one who upholds his proof”—and he pointed to al-Ḥasan (عليه السلام)—“and I bear witness that al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī is the وصي of his brother and the one who upholds his proof after him.”

And I bear witness concerning ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn that he is the one who upholds the affair of al-Ḥusayn after him. And I bear witness concerning Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī that he is the one who upholds the affair of ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn. And I bear witness concerning Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad that he is the one who upholds the affair of Muḥammad. And I bear witness concerning Mūsā that he is the one who upholds the affair of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. And I bear witness concerning ʿAlī ibn Mūsā that he is the one who upholds the affair of Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar. And I bear witness concerning Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī that he is the one who upholds the affair of ʿAlī ibn Mūsā. And I bear witness concerning ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad that he is the one who upholds the affair of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī.

And I bear witness concerning al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī that he is the one who upholds the affair of ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad. And I bear witness concerning a man from the offspring of al-Ḥasan, who is neither given a teknonym nor named until his affair becomes manifest; then he will fill it with justice just as it had been filled with injustice. And peace be upon you, O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings.”

Then he stood and departed. So Amīr al-Muʾminīn said: “O Abā Muḥammad, follow him and see where he is heading.” So al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام) went out and said: “It was only that he placed his foot outside the mosque, and I did not know where he had gone in the earth of Allah.” So I returned to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام) and informed him. He said: “O Abā Muḥammad, do you know him?” I said: “Allah, His Messenger, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn know best.” He said: “He is al-Khiḍr (عليه السلام).”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام), presented here as the rightful divine authority.
key_terms.الْأَخْوَالَ: The maternal uncles, referenced in resemblance of offspring.
key_terms.الْأَعْمَامَ: The paternal uncles, referenced in resemblance of offspring.
key_terms.الْخَضِرُ: Al-Khiḍr (عليه السلام), identified as the mysterious visitor.
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ بِحُجَّتِهِ: The one who upholds the divine proof and authority after the previous Imam.
key_terms.رُوحُهُ: His spirit, mentioned in the question about sleep and the state of the soul.
key_terms.عَدْلًا: Justice, describing how the final Imam will fill the earth.
key_terms.وَصِيُّ: The designated successor entrusted with religious authority after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith from al-Kāfī present the names and succession of the twelve Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a meeting in al-Masjid al-Ḥarām in which a mysterious man tests Amīr al-Muʾminīn (عليه السلام), then bears witness to the succession of the twelve Imams. The report is significant in Shia creed for its explicit designation of the Imams and its conclusion that the visitor was al-Khiḍr (عليه السلام), affirming their divine authority and the awaited rise of the final Imam.
